topic: The Pi-Collision Mystery: Counting Collisions to Calculate Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school students or curious science enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: The Impossible Counting Puzzle
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
A small mass hits a massive block.
The wall reflects the smaller block back.
Number of collisions encodes Pi's digits.
The mass difference controls the precision.

Animate the small mass approaching the large [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg].
Show the small mass bouncing off the large [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg].
Represent each collision with a digit popping up.
Scale the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg]s dynamically to visualize mass ratios.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Elastic collisions obey strict conservation laws.
Momentum remains constant during every impact.
Kinetic energy is perfectly preserved throughout.
animations: Draw two vectors representing velocity components in #33A1FF near the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/billiard.svg].
Show the conservation of momentum equation: m1v1 + m2v2 = const.
Display the kinetic energy equation: 1/2mv^2 = const.

sections.title: Mapping Physics to Geometry
lecture_lines: We transform velocities into a 2D plane.
Collisions trace a path in phase space.
Boundaries reflect the path to form circles.
animations: Create a 2D coordinate system labeled #FFFFFF using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg] for precision.
Plot the velocity vector path tracing a curve.
Add reflecting lines using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mirror.svg] that force the path into a circle.
Animate the path hitting boundaries and turning.
Highlight the center of the circle in #FF33FF, measuring the radius with a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg].

sections.title: The Emergence of Pi
lecture_lines: Bounces follow the arc of a circle.
Reflections equate to Pi's geometric ratio.
Mass ratios determine the number of digits.
Pi emerges from these simple physical dynamics.
Higher mass ratios reveal more Pi digits.
animations: Draw a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] circle with radius defined by mass ratios.
Show the collision path as a sequence of bounces using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg].
Display the ratio of arc lengths to total circumference.
Fade in the digits of Pi one by one.
Show the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] circle growing as the mass ratio increases.

sections.title: Conclusion & Summary
lecture_lines: Pi hides in physical dynamic systems.
Mass ratios link physics to geometry.
Simple collisions reveal deep mathematical constants.
